headline: Early Signs of Growth Revival, as margins remain a key monitorable; Domestic business the underdog…

highlights: International services EBITDA margin improved marginally by 10bps q/q to 15.5%, even as utilisation increased 200bps to 90.5%, partially offset by wage hikes, one time severance costs and AI investments.
We believe the Q shows early signs of stabilisation translating into growth, although the recovery remains modest and uneven across accounts.
Management's commentary suggests a gradual shift from defending the existing revenue base towards capturing incremental AI-led transformation spending.

Legacy modernisation, AI-powered engineering and AI-ready data contributed ~61% of incremental pipeline, while AI-led order book increased 11.3% q/q to $24.2mn (~25% of total order book), with pipeline reaching $358mn (+5% q/q).
valuation: Outlook & Valuation: At CMP, the stock trades at FY28/29e P/E of 12.6x/11.6x.
We retain a BUY rating, with a TP of Rs. 304, implying ~27% upside from CMP.
Life sciences currently has the most mature pipeline among the targeted new sub-verticals. ◼ RMD: Retail remains under pressure and could take another 1–2 quarters to recover.
watch: Outlook & Valuation: At CMP, the stock trades at FY28/29e P/E of 12.6x/11.6x.

Key Risks: Further large-account ramp-downs, particularly in BFSI and TMT vertical; Delayed AI-led deal conversion and continued solution investments; Prolonged enterprise decision cycles and weak large-client progression; Continued Data and Retail weakness; and Slower monetisation of domestic hyperscaler partnerships.
